title: Write about your yesterday
writingModel: Yesterday was Thursday, the fifteenth of October. The weather was cool but dry — there was a pale blue sky above the WKU campus. It was a busy day from start to finish. I want to describe it as clearly as I can, because it was one of those ordinary days that turn out to be important.

In the morning, I was at my first lecture at eight o'clock sharp. The topic was the history of international law. Our professor, Dr. Nurgali, was excellent — his explanations were clear and his examples were memorable. I was completely focused and my notes were detailed. After the lecture, there was a fifteen-minute break. I was in the corridor with Asel. She was tired because the lecture was early and her dormitory was far from the main building.

At lunchtime, the WKU cafeteria was busy as usual. The menu was simple but very satisfying: there was rice with chicken and fresh salad. The portions were generous and the prices were very affordable for students. I was at a table with three classmates from my Law group. The mood was relaxed and there were a lot of laughs. For thirty minutes, we were not students — we were just friends.

In the afternoon, there was a group study session in the university library. The topic was contract law — a complex but fascinating area of study. There were four of us: me, Asel, Marat, and Timur. The session was productive and useful. The library was quiet and the atmosphere was calm. At the end, I was satisfied. The material was difficult, but we were all a little bit wiser.

In the evening, I was in my dormitory room by seven o'clock. I was on the phone with my parents in Taraz for about half an hour. My mother was happy to hear my voice. My younger brother was at a football match — he was so excited and loud in the background! After the call, I was tired but content. I was in bed by ten. Overall, yesterday was a good, productive, ordinary day. And sometimes, those are the very best days of all.
